items.title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
items.rawSummary:
Widgets, your way. | Photo: Allison Johnson / The Verge	

Aside from dealing with my calendar, there's one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I'm about to miss the bus.
What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house. Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and select my stop will slow me down enough to miss a bus. I need glanceable information, and I hoped that Android's vibe-coded widget feature could help me out here. It hasn't, to my disappointment, but I still had a good time cooking up other widgets.

Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
items.rawSummary: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the U.S. tightens its push to keep AI chips out of China.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue
